summary: Build-2 (page) of #57 is done; ./check.sh is green, node www/play-read.mjs passes, and `cd merge4 && npm test` prints archived. Added: a 'Why' list (select.js whyHtml, up to rules.notes_shown from Sim.notes) in the clan, market, camp, scout and capital panels; tile panels and tooltips name a camp holding the tile and a clan's tile as home/territory/route; MapView.setFocus (selected clan's territory and route bright, others dim) and setHomeLine (the player's camp's line, thin and faint, always); View > Hidden country (v-country, key H, off by default) gates the closed-country outlines, the tooltip/panel zone name and the legend rows; feed.js has an alerts box (last 5, clickable), alert styling ('!' and red left border) and an unread count on the Feed button; the load error shows in #error. merge4/ holds only README.md and package.json; its row is out of the repo README. www/play-read.mjs is in engine/CLAUDE.md. Screenshots in relay/specs/57/screens/: clan-why.png, camp-why.png, country-on.png, alerts.png. In alerts.png the first alert shown was a rival's clan joining, not camp hunger, since the run stops at the first alert.

decisions.decision: The alerts box rows show the kind icon and a '!' before the text; the feed list also puts '!' before alert text.
decisions.why: The spec says '!' before the text; keeping the kind icon too lets alerts keep their kind's look.

decisions.decision: Selecting a tile with a clan (chosen or in whose territory) sets the focus; selecting anything else clears it.
decisions.why: Spec item 14: a tile panel with a clan.

decisions.decision: Added game.notes(id) on window.game for the play script.
decisions.why: play-read.mjs picks the clan with the most reasons so the screenshot reads.

ideas.title: docs/design cites merge4/ paths
ideas.body: merge4/ is archived; design files that cite merge4/... paths are the owner's to update, and ci.yml's js matrix can drop merge4.

ideas.title: play-read could wait for a camp alert
ideas.body: The script stops at the first alert of any kind; it could require a camp hunger or cut-line alert to shoot the most telling box.
